what: M1 early-mapping acceptance after the identity-map change (TTBR0 instead of TTBR1)

on.meaning: the identity-map L1 entry for the framebuffer's block is not a table

reading: No fault and no regression: the identity-map version refuses instead of breaking the boot, which is what the TTBR1 version could not do (build 45969556167 removed the console).

State 5 says the identity map does not cover the framebuffer's block at all under QEMU, because start.s maps only the kernel's own physical range; the boot arguments' video base (0xEC7A0000 here) is outside it.

The walk also has a naming problem to settle before the next build: with a 4 KB granule the TTBR points at the root (L0) and the byte range is chosen at L1, so indexing TTBR0 with the L1 mask is only correct on the 16 KB granule. The next version has to follow ARM_TT_ROOT_* first and then ARM_TT_L1_*, exactly as the TTBR1 version did when it moved from state 2 to 7.

conclusion.early_map_path: safe refusal (5); nothing drawn; mapping not installed
conclusion.next_step: walk root then L1 in the identity map and only then fill the block entry, still refusing when an index is out of range or a slot holds a different block
